issues.problem: The supplied mechanical_design_errors still repeat the prior complaint ('target/candidate role X must name only the referent table channel_members; intermediate records belong in support roles'), but the roles in this revision have already been restructured: each *_cm role is entity CONVERSATION_MEMBERSHIP with facts limited to the membership's own composite key (user+channel), and the timezone fact has been moved out into a separate paired *_user support role (entity USER) bound on the same user_id, exactly as binding_note specifies. On inspection the flagged defect from the prior iteration appears resolved; the error list looks stale/unregenerated rather than a fresh finding against this corrected role split.
issues.repair: Re-run the mechanical check against the current role definitions; if it still flags priya_cm etc., clarify whether naming the user_id/channel_id that constitutes the membership row's own key counts as an 'intermediate record' (it should not, since that is the referent entity's identity, not a borrowed attribute from USER).

rationale: The prompt, route (CONVERSATION_MEMBERSHIP→USER), and multiple-resolution mode are unchanged and remain justified: the request is a plain filtered membership listing needing both the channel-scoped membership fact and the linked user's timezone attribute. The binding_note and role list now correctly separate each qualifying person into a CONVERSATION_MEMBERSHIP match role (membership in C_INFRA) and a paired USER support role (timezone), bound on the same user_id, which is the proper way to carry a cross-entity filter condition into a single-entity referent. Cross-checking against the base seed confirms the six matches (Priya, Lukas, Sophie, Olena, Kenji, Aisha) all hold core-infra membership with non-US timezones, and the four negatives exercise distinct, real failure modes: two US-timezone members (Mateo, Robert), a member with no stored timezone (the bot), and a user with a qualifying timezone but membership in the wrong channel (Incognito). No hidden-ID reliance; the access_plan uses only documented conversations.list/members and users.info calls. The single open point is that the supplied mechanical_design_errors list textually still names the pre-fix defect even though the role structure in this version appears to have already corrected it, which is worth re-verifying but does not itself indicate an actual remaining flaw in the visible design.
